---
title: "Single-table functions"
---

## Rows

`filter()` keeps rows where every condition is true. Conditions are row
closures, vector helpers such as `between()` or `if_any()`, or the name of a
logical column. NA counts as false. `filter_out()` drops the rows where every
condition is true and keeps rows where a condition is NA, so `filter()` and
`filter_out()` with the same conditions split a table without overlap.

{{< include ../examples/_filter.md >}}

In a grouped table, the second closure argument is the row's group, and vector
helpers are evaluated per group:

{{< include ../examples/_filter-grouped.md >}}

`arrange()` sorts rows. It is stable and puts NA last. Keys are column names,
`desc()`, or expressions, which are evaluated over the whole table. It ignores
grouping unless you pass `_by_group: true`.

{{< include ../examples/_arrange.md >}}

`distinct()` keeps unique rows over the given columns, or over all columns.
Named arguments add computed columns first, and `_keep_all: true` keeps every
column from the first row of each combination.

The slice family picks rows within each group:

| Function | Rows |
| --- | --- |
| `slice(1, 3)`, `slice(-1)` | By 1-based position; negative positions drop rows. |
| `slice_head(n:)`, `slice_tail(n:)` | The first or last rows. |
| `slice_min(x, n:)`, `slice_max(x, n:)` | The rows with the smallest or largest values, with ties kept unless `with_ties: false`. |
| `slice_sample(n:, replace:, weight_by:)` | Random rows. Seed with `mt_srand()`. |
| `head(n)` | The first rows of the whole table, ignoring groups. |
| `top_n(n, wt)`, `top_frac(prop, wt)` | Superseded by `slice_max()`. Rows ranked within `n`, in table order. |
| `sample_n(size)`, `sample_frac(size)` | Superseded by `slice_sample()`. |
| `add_row(x: 1, _before:, _after:)` | New rows of values; columns not given are NA. |

Each takes `prop:` in place of `n:`, and `_by:`.

{{< include ../examples/_slice.md >}}

## Columns

`select()` keeps columns by name or with [tidyselect helpers](tidyselect.qmd).
An associative array renames while selecting. `rename()` renames with
`new: 'old'` arguments, `rename_with()` applies a function to selected names,
and `relocate()` moves columns to the front or `_before` / `_after` another
column.

{{< include ../examples/_select.md >}}

`mutate()` adds or replaces columns. A value can be a row closure, a vector
helper, a list with one value per row, a scalar, or `null` to drop the column.
Later arguments see the columns made by earlier ones.

{{< include ../examples/_mutate.md >}}

`mutate()` takes dplyr's options: `_by` groups for one call, `_keep: 'none'`
keeps only the grouping and new columns, and `_before` or `_after` place the
new columns. `transmute()` is `mutate()` that keeps only the new columns.

{{< include ../examples/_mutate-options.md >}}

`pull()` returns one column as a PHP list. It takes a name or a position
(1-based, negative from the end, the last column by default) and an optional
`name:` column whose values become the keys.

{{< include ../examples/_distinct-pull.md >}}

## Summaries

`summarise()` returns one row per group. Each named argument is a summary
helper or a closure that receives the group's table and returns one value.
With several grouping columns, the result drops the last one, as in dplyr.
`_groups` accepts `'drop_last'`, `'drop'`, `'keep'`, and `'rowwise'`.

{{< include ../examples/_summarise.md >}}

`reframe()` is `summarise()` for summaries that return several values. Results
are recycled to a common length within each group, and the output is
ungrouped.

{{< include ../examples/_reframe.md >}}

`count()` counts rows per combination of columns within any existing groups and
keeps the original grouping. `wt:` sums a column instead, `sort: true` orders by
the count, and `name:` names the count column. `tally()` counts within the
current groups, and `add_count()` and `add_tally()` add the count as a column.

{{< include ../examples/_count.md >}}

`glimpse()` prints a compact summary of each column and returns the table
unchanged.
